messages:
sam: Heads up — ran a full suite this morning and saw a regression on small-batch decode after the new fused/paged FlashAttention variant landed on canary. Prefill numbers look stable, decode p95 for batch_size=1 jumped from ~42ms -> ~78ms on the same instance type.

maria: Ouch. Which model + seq len / hw?

sam: gpt-medium-ish (1.2B), seq_len=32, GPU=A100-80GB, driver/torch same as last week. Workload: continuous small-batch decode (streaming). We started getting a bursty KV cache eviction pattern in the profiler. Miss rate up 2% -> 8%.

aj: Can you paste the minimal repro command? I can run a microbench locally.

sam: repro script is:```
./bench/decode_run.sh --model rdx/gpt-1.2b --variant flash-paged-fused --batch 1 --seq 32 --iters 1000
```

sam: Perf log excerpt (from trace):```
[decode_step] total_ms=78.3
  kernel: flash_paged_fused_attn  34.1ms
  kernel: kv_page_wifi_copy      12.7ms
  kernel: small_matmul_tail       9.4ms
  memcpy H2D/D2H combined         8.6ms
  scheduler overhead              6.5ms
```

perf-bot: :warning: Canary alert: decode_p95 increased 85% for variant flash-paged-fused on pool rdx-canary-eu-2. See /deployments/21265 for details.

maria: Interesting that memcpy shows up. Paged attention can introduce extra page-level copies if alignment is off or if we fallback to thread-local buffers. Any recent kv_page_size changes merged?

aj: I bisected locally: when I flip off fusion (keep paged but non-fused Flash kernels) latency goes back down to ~45ms. So fusion seems to be the change triggering extra memory traffic for tiny batches. Hypothesis: fused kernel expects larger effective batch concat and is materializing KV pages in a way that prevents prefix cache hits from being in-GPU-L2.

sam: That matches the KV eviction pattern — more full-page writes causing L2 evictions and higher memcpy counts. We also see a small increase in CUDA-launch count which matches microkernel fragmentation.

infra: Quick mitigation would be to add a heuristic: prefer non-fused flash variant for decode when batch_size<=2 OR when avg_seq<=64. We can roll that flag to canary quickly.

maria: Another lever: try reducing kv_page_size from 64k -> 32k for the fused path so pages are better packed and less likely to stomp. But that could increase page table churn. Need microbench.

aj: I'll run a quick A/B: (A) fused+32k page, (B) non-fused default. Will post numbers.

sam: Thank you. If A works, we might keep fusion but tune page size; if B wins, revert fusion for small-batch decode until we fix memory layout.

aj: Results:
A (fused + 32k): decode_p95=50.2ms, KV_miss=3.5%, memcpy down 60%
B (non-fused): decode_p95=44.8ms, KV_miss=2.1%, memcpy minimal

maria: So A improves a lot vs current, but B is still best. For throughput workloads fusion still helps. So strategy: route small-batch decode to non-fused variant, leave fused/paged for prefill and large-batch. Add config flags:```
"kernel_routing": {
  "decode_small_batch": {
    "max_batch": 2,
    "prefer": "flash-nonfused"
  },
  "paged_fused_default": {
    "kv_page_size": 65536
  }
}
```

sam: Can infra push a canary with the routing change? We should verify with streaming traffic.

infra: Canary deploy started: `deployctl roll canary --service inference --config routing_small_batch=true`

perf-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary run (30m) shows decode_p95 back to 47ms on canary pool, error rate unchanged.

maria: Awesome. I'll open a follow-up to track longer-term fixes: (1) investigate kernel memory layout to remove extra memcpy for fused path, (2) tune page allocator to minimize eviction thrash, (3) add unit microbench for <3 batch decode paths so we catch regressions earlier.

sam: Filed: https://tracker/redwood/INF-3241 — notes + flamegraphs attached.

aj: Also adding a perf-test that runs fused vs non-fused under continuous batching at small-batch sizes (streaming emulation).

sam: Thanks all. Good rollback+routing plan for now. :tada:

maria: follow-up: let's also add an observability metric exposing memcpy_ms_per_decode_step so the alerting can be more targeted.

infra: noted — will add metric and dashboard tile on per-route view.

sam: closing thread when infra confirms metric and deploy stable.
